title: Resilience plan for regional routing loop triggered by TTL/KV eviction mismatch
creator: Lena Park
description: Summary: On 2026-02-14 ~11:40 UTC a production capacity perturbation in us-west caused a routing oscillation across regions that amplified into a degraded tail-latency event for a subset of customers using dedicated pools. Detection: alerted by Console SLO alerts (p95 latency spike) and increased error-rate traces from router service. Impact: ~12% requests experienced elevated latency or 5xx errors for 18 minutes before automated dampening reduced oscillation. Root cause (high level): a timing mismatch between routing policy propagation (short TTL delta) and per-node KV cache eviction / tombstone handling allowed stale variant bindings to survive in some edge routers. When autoscaler signals reduced local capacity, smart-routing quickly promoted a remote variant; that remote promotion invalidated local cache entries but eviction windows overlapped with stale policy entries, causing bidirectional reroutes. Secondary factor: the fallback selector preferred a size-compatible variant (quantized) that had incomplete handshake metadata for kernel compatibility, producing transient model load errors and triggering further failovers. Why this is unique: the incident was not a single bug in policy code but a systems-level race between policy replication, KV cache lifecycle, and variant compatibility checks under bursty capacity signals.
comments: 2026-02-15: Initial triage by oncall. Collected router traces, KV cache histograms, autoscaler events. Noted correlation between policy propagation events and cache eviction spikes. -- Lena Park
2026-02-17: Engineering diagnosis completed. Root cause identified as TTL + eviction window race and missing 'compatibility handshake' in variant metadata. Draft action items proposed. -- Raj Patel

2026-02-20: Design review with runtime team. Agreed on three-pronged fix: (1) conservative policy-version handshake, (2) KV cache tombstone and grace window, (3) stricter compatibility gating for fallback variants. -- Marco Ruiz (runtime lead)

2026-02-23: Implemented temporary mitigation: increase policy TTL delta to 120s and enable routing dampening flags in prod; oscillation reduced immediately per dashboards. Mitigation will remain until hard fixes land. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/4821 -- Raj Patel

2026-02-26: Code reviews started for KV eviction grace window and compat handshake; unit tests added for cross-region failover scenarios. Performance team requested microbenchmark before merge. -- Aisha Khan

2026-03-01: Draft runbook updates created for oncall to detect TTL/eviction mismatch and apply dampening. Postmortem doc linked in attachments. Next: rollout hard fixes in canary region and run chaos test. -- Raj Patel
action_items: A1: Add policy-version handshake to routing agents so a router will ignore policy changes until it confirms KV store sweep completed. Owner: Raj Patel. Due: 2026-03-10.
A2: Implement KV cache tombstone with configurable grace window and telemetry for eviction skews. Owner: Aisha Khan. Due: 2026-03-08.
A3: Add explicit kernel/format compatibility metadata and gating in fallback selector to avoid loading incompatible variants. Owner: Marco Ruiz. Due: 2026-03-12.
A4: Create a chaos test that simulates rapid capacity oscillations + delayed policy propagation to validate fixes. Owner: SRE team (contact: Diego Morales). Due: 2026-03-18.
A5: Update Console SLO dashboard to include 'policy-propagation-lag' and 'kv-eviction-lag' panels and an alert that ties to routing-dampening toggle. Owner: Observability team. Due: 2026-03-05.
A6: Temporary mitigation retention: keep routing dampening flags enabled and policy TTL increased until rollout complete. Owner: Oncall rotation. Due: 2026-03-15 (review).
